Summary: First Corinthians 13 is the Bible's great hymn to love, written to a church that had gifts but no grace. Paul insists that without love, even the most spectacular spirituality is noise. This passage study works through the chapter's three movements — love's necessity, love's character, love's permanence — so you can measure your own life by love's standard.
Steps: Read the chapter in context first (1 Corinthians 12-14), so you see why Paul wrote about love to this church; Study verses 1-3, asking what impressive things are worthless without love — and where you chase them; Work through the qualities in verses 4-7 one by one, testing yourself against each; Compare the chapter's picture of love with your closest relationship, honestly; Study verses 8-13, asking why love remains when gifts and knowledge pass away; End by rewriting verses 4-7 with your own name, and praying it as a confession
Questions: Why does Paul place this chapter between two chapters about spiritual gifts — what problem was he solving?; Which quality of love in verses 4-7 is hardest for you — patience, kindness, humility, forgiveness?; What is the difference between love as a feeling and love as Paul describes it?; How does this chapter challenge the way you use your own gifts and strengths?; What would your church, family, or workplace look like if it were marked by this kind of love?
Application: Pick the one quality of love you most lack, and practice it deliberately toward one person every day this week.
